statement.p: A closed rectangular box with faces parallel to the coordinate planes has one bottom corner at the origin and the opposite top corner in the first octant on the plane 3 x + 4 y + z = 1. What is the maximum volume of such a box?

static.solution:
(x,y,z), the volume of the box is V=xyz. Since z=1 - 3 x - 4 y on the plane, the volume is given by V=xy (1 - 3 x - 4 y) = xy - 3 x^2 y - 4 xy^2. The domain is the triangular region 0\leq x\leq \frac{1}{3}, 0\leq y \leq (1 - 3 x)/4. At a critical point, \frac{\partial V}{\partial x} = y - 6 xy - 4 y^2 = y(1- x- 4 y) = 0, and \frac{\partial V}{\partial y} = x - 3 x^2 - 8 xy = x(1 - 3 x- 8 y) = 0. One solution is x=y=0. Another is x=0, y=\frac{1}{4}; another is y=0, x=\frac{1}{3}. Another is the solution of 1 - 6 x - 4 y = 0, \qquad 1 - 3 x - 8 y =0, namely x=\frac{1}{9}, y=\frac{1}{12}.
If either x=0 or y=0, then V=0, so these solutions do not give the maximum volume. Since D=V_{xx}V_{yy}-(V_{xy})^2 = (-6 y)(-8 x) - (1 - 6 x - 8 y)^2, at the remaining critical point we have D\left ( \frac{1}{9}, \frac{1}{12}\right ) = \left(-6 \cdot\frac1{12}\right) \left(-8\cdot\frac1{9}\right) - \left(1 - 6\cdot\frac1{9} - 8\cdot\frac1{12}\right)^2 = \frac{4}{9}-\frac{1}{9}=\frac{1}{3}>0, and V_{xx}(\frac1{9},\frac1{12})=-\frac{1}{2}\lt 0, the point x=\frac{1}{9},\, y=\frac{1}{12}, is a local maximum at which V= (1/9)(1/12) - 3(1/9)^2(1/12) - 4(1/9)(1/12)^2 = 1/324.
Since all points on the boundary of the domain give V=0, the local maximum is a global maximum.
